title: Publish-Subscribe

canonical_reuse.historical_import: docs/pattern-packages/data-engineering/import.json remains unchanged; its hashes describe the original import, not this revision.

validation.research: Six primary sources: Hohpe and Woolf’s Publish-Subscribe Channel and Competing Consumers catalogs, Microsoft Publisher-Subscriber guidance, Redis delivery semantics, Google Cloud subscription overview, and AWS SNS-to-SQS documentation. Independent subscriptions are distinguished from workers sharing one subscription; retention, acknowledgment, ordering, and recovery contracts are attributed to specific implementations rather than claimed universally.

runnable_example.verification: Independent fan-out/FIFO progress, shared workers, capacity without partial enqueue, topic isolation, no history, duplicate publication, destructive loss, cleanup/deletion, immutable payload, and validation checks passed.

example_limits: Original sequential in-memory model with exact topics, unique subscription names, immutable message values, pending-message capacity, FIFO take, no subscribers returning zero, no replay, and destructive queue deletion. Preflight full-queue rejection changes no queue in this sequential example; it is not crash-atomic fan-out. Take removes a message immediately, so a later worker failure loses that delivery. Duplicate publication is not deduplicated. No network, acknowledgments, retry protocol, thread safety, persistent storage, access controls, or source-transaction integration. Managed SNS-to-SQS is an explanatory second context only.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, commit, push, or pull request.
